paras.en: Sanders: I understood a bit more about what Patrick meant about feeling isolated. I stopped trying to connect. I self-censored. I didn’t have to stop. After all, I had the technology to communicate in my literal hand, but it felt too hard, too slow, too artificial. It didn’t feel like it was worth the effort for me to type and to ask other people to slow down and listen. My brief experiment gave me a glimpse, a tiny glimpse, into a life without a voice.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我对帕特里克感到孤立的含义有了更多的了解。我停止尝试连接。我自我审查。我不必停下来。毕竟，我拥有可以用我的双手进行交流的技术，但感觉太难、太慢、太人工。我觉得不值得我费力打字并要求其他人放慢速度倾听。我短暂的实验让我瞥见了一个没有声音的生活。

paras.en: Piotrowski: Being able to ask for things, being able to tell someone when you are in pain. Or when you’re feeling good, or when something that they do is helpful.
paras.zh: Piotrowski：能够提出要求，能够在痛苦时告诉别人。或者当你感觉良好时，或者当他们做的事情有帮助时。

paras.en: Sanders: Speech-language pathologist Jessica Piotrowski works at the UC Davis Center for Voice and Swallowing. She helps people who are losing their ability to talk.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：言语病理学家杰西卡·皮奥特罗斯基在加州大学戴维斯分校声音和吞咽中心工作。她帮助那些失去说话能力的人。

paras.en: Pietrowski: The interesting thing that I have learned in working in this field, and I’m not sure if the general public is aware, is that for many of these individuals, losing their speech is way more devastating than losing their mobility. You know, you think you think about what these individuals often are unfortunately losing: their mobility, their independence, their swallowing. But being able to communicate is going to, in some way, help them a little bit through all those things. And going through all of those changes without a voice or a way to kind of be yourself just makes them so much harder and just to be able to express yourself and to maintain a little more of a sense of dignity of like, this is who I am. This disease is not going to take that. I still have my voice. I still have my sense of humor. I still have my emotion that I can hopefully in the coming future express to people. It’s just so, so important.
paras.zh: 彼得罗夫斯基：我在这一领域的工作中学到的一件有趣的事情是，对于其中许多人来说，失去言语比失去行动能力更具破坏性，我不确定公众是否意识到这一点。你知道，你想想这些人经常不幸失去的东西：他们的行动能力、他们的独立性、他们的吞咽能力。但能够沟通将在某种程度上帮助他们解决所有这些问题。在没有声音或没有办法做自己的情况下经历所有这些变化只会让它们变得更加困难，而只是能够表达自己并保持更多的尊严感，这就是我。这种疾病不会接受这个。我仍然有我的声音。我仍然有我的幽默感。我仍然有我的情感，希望在不久的将来能够向人们表达。这就是如此、如此重要。

paras.en: Sanders: In 2022, two years after his ALS diagnosis, Jules’ voice started slipping away. MA had already thought about this inevitable moment, and she was dreading it.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：2022 年，即朱尔斯诊断出 ALS 两年后，朱尔斯的声音开始消失。妈妈已经想到了这个不可避免的时刻，她很害怕它。

paras.en: MA: Thinking back when I was at that time, and he was losing all of his physical abilities, you know, little by little, it’s like, you can no longer do this, and then that, and then that, and then that. And I always remember thinking, all of these things are breaking my heart, but when he loses his voice, I’m just going to shatter into a million pieces.
paras.zh: 马：回想我当时的情况，他的身体能力都在丧失，你知道，一点一点地，你不能再做这个，然后那个，然后那个，然后那个。我总是记得我在想，所有这些事情都让我心碎，但当他失去声音时，我就会碎成一百万块。

paras.en: Sanders: On the next episode of Talk To Me.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在《跟我说话》的下一集里。

paras.en: MA: I still remember the first time, this was in 2022, the summer of 22, that I heard the first little crack in his voice that let me know something’s changing.
paras.zh: MA：我还记得第一次，那是在 2022 年，也就是 22 号的夏天，我听到他声音中的第一个小裂痕，让我知道有些事情正在发生变化。

paras.en: Sanders: What does it feel like to stare down a future without a voice, especially for Jules? On his long-running podcast with MA, they talk about their lives, their family, their life that they’re building. They also talk about his ALS.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在没有声音的情况下展望未来是什么感觉，尤其是对朱尔斯来说？在他与 MA 的长期播客中，他们谈论他们的生活、他们的家庭、他们正在建设的生活。他们还谈论了他的 ALS。

paras.en: Jules: It’s strange with the podcast because you can hear my real voice slowly decay till we stop.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：播客很奇怪，因为你可以听到我真实的声音慢慢衰减，直到我们停止。

paras.en: MA: Yeah, it really is this archive of what he sounded like little by little as it changed. And it was, yeah, like very disarming to get to that moment. And then you begin to get used to it, and you sort of work around it and you appreciate that it’s still there. But that was, yeah, that was really, really difficult for me.
paras.zh: MA：是的，这确实是他听起来一点一点改变的档案。是的，那一刻让人非常放松。然后你开始习惯它，你可以解决它，你会感激它仍然存在。但这对我来说真的非常困难。

paras.en: Sanders: How much of Jules was his voice?
paras.zh: 桑德斯：他的声音有多少是朱尔斯的？

paras.en: Jules: For me, it felt like I was fading away. Like when Marty McFly was seeing his family fade away in the picture he had in “Back to the Future.”
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：对我来说，感觉就像我正在消失。就像马蒂·麦克弗莱在《回到未来》的照片中看到他的家人逐渐消失一样。

paras.en: Sanders: This is The Deep End, Season 2, Talk to Me. I’m Laura Sanders. If you liked this podcast, tell your friends. If you really like this podcast, leave us a review. It helps the show a lot. Send us your questions and your comments at podcasts at sciencenews.org.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：《这里是深渊》第二季，《跟我说话》。我是劳拉·桑德斯。如果您喜欢这个播客，请告诉您的朋友。如果您真的喜欢这个播客，请给我们留下评论。对节目帮助很大。通过 sciencenews.org 的播客向我们发送您的问题和评论。

paras.en: The Deep End is a production of Science News. It’s based on original reporting by me, Laura Sanders. This episode was produced and mixed by Ella Rowen. Our project manager is Ashley Yeager. Nancy Shute is our editor-in-chief. Our music is by Blue Dot Sessions. The podcast is made possible in part by the Burroughs Wellcome Fund with support from PRX.
paras.zh: 《The Deep End》是《科学新闻》的制作。它基于我劳拉·桑德斯的原创报道。本集由 Ella Rowen 制作和混音。我们的项目经理是阿什利·耶格尔。南希·舒特 (Nancy Shute) 是我们的主编。我们的音乐是由 Blue Dot Sessions 制作的。该播客的部分制作是由 Burroughs Wellcome 基金在 PRX 的支持下完成的。

paras.en: This podcast was produced with support from the Burroughs Wellcome Fund and in partnership with PRX. The podcast logo was created by Neil Webb.
paras.zh: 该播客是在 Burroughs Wellcome 基金的支持下并与 PRX 合作制作的。播客徽标由尼尔·韦伯创建。

articles.title: Here’s a look at the Nobel Prizes for science
articles.author: Nikk Ogasa

paras.en: It’s Nobels season — that time of the year when we find out which groundbreaking, paradigm-shifting, world-changing achievements beat out the rest to win what is arguably the most prestigious award on Earth.
paras.zh: 现在是诺贝尔奖季——一年中的这个时候，我们会找出哪些突破性、范式转变、改变世界的成就击败其他成就，赢得可以说是地球上最负盛名的奖项。

paras.en: From a light switch for the brain to the discovery of an ultra-elusive subatomic particle hailing from beyond our solar system to a solution to one of the most enduring puzzles in all of organic chemistry, the researchers behind this year’s scientific prizes each revolutionized the ways that scientists understand the world around them.
paras.zh: 从大脑的光开关到发现来自太阳系之外的极其难以捉摸的亚原子粒子，再到解决有机化学中最持久的难题之一，今年科学奖项背后的研究人员都彻底改变了科学家理解周围世界的方式。

paras.en: Take a look at the science behind each of this year’s awards.
paras.zh: 看看今年每个奖项背后的科学原理。

paras.en: A galaxy of nearly 90 billion neurons exists within a single human brain. But unlike stars in the void, neurons communicate with one another via some 100 trillion connections, allowing the human mind to learn, adapt and interact with its surroundings.
paras.zh: 一个人脑内存在一个由近 900 亿个神经元组成的星系。但与虚空中的星星不同的是，神经元通过约 100 万亿个连接相互通信，使人类思维能够学习、适应周围环境并与之互动。

paras.en: For scientists to understand how individual actions arise from such complexity, they needed a tool to directly link neural circuits to specific behaviors, said Abdel El Manira, a neuroscientist at the Karolinska Institute in Stockholm. “Neuroscientists dreamed of a neuronal switch, a tool to turn specific neurons on or off with great precision,” El Manira said during the Oct. 5 announcement of this year’s prize in physiology or medicine by the Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institute.
paras.zh: 斯德哥尔摩卡罗林斯卡研究所的神经科学家阿卜杜勒·埃尔·马尼拉 (Abdel El Manira) 表示，为了让科学家了解个体行为如何从如此复杂的情况中产生，他们需要一种工具将神经回路与特定行为直接联系起来。 “神经科学家梦想有一个神经元开关，一种能够非常精确地打开或关闭特定神经元的工具，”埃尔·马尼拉在卡罗林斯卡学院诺贝尔大会 10 月 5 日宣布今年的生理学或医学奖时说道。

paras.en: Enter the bright idea that won. It’s a technology called optogenetics, which involves using light to precisely activate specific cells, like neurons, and watch how behavior changes. For their foundational contributions to optogenetics, biophysicists Peter Hegemann of Humboldt University in Berlin and Georg Nagel, of the Julius-Maximilians-Universität Würzburg in Germany, and neuroscientist Karl Deisseroth of Stanford University shared this year’s prize.
paras.zh: 输入获胜的好主意。这是一种称为光遗传学的技术，涉及利用光精确激活特定细胞（例如神经元），并观察行为如何变化。柏林洪堡大学的生物物理学家 Peter Hegemann 和德国维尔茨堡朱利叶斯·马克西米利安大学的 Georg Nagel 以及斯坦福大学的神经科学家 Karl Deisseroth 分享了今年的奖项，以表彰他们对光遗传学的基础性贡献。

paras.en: The prize winners’ story starts in an unlikely place: the eye spot of a single celled green alga called Chlamydomonas. In the early 2000s, Hegemann, then at the Max Planck Institute for Biochemistry in Martinsreid, Germany, and Nagel, at the Max Planck Institute for Biophysics in Frankfurt, discovered a unique protein in the alga’s eye spot. When illuminated, the protein generated an electrical impulse, enabling the organism to move. Further research revealed that when the protein, called channelrhodopsin, was exposed to light, it opened like a pore, allowing positively charged ions to flow into a cell, generating the electrical impulse. “They had just discovered the switch neuroscientists had long dreamed of,” El Manira said.
paras.zh: 获奖者的故事始于一个意想不到的地方：一种称为衣藻的单细胞绿藻的眼点。 2000 年代初，当时在德国马丁斯里德马克斯普朗克生物化学研究所工作的赫格曼和在法兰克福马克斯普朗克生物物理研究所工作的内格尔在藻类的眼斑中发现了一种独特的蛋白质。当光照时，蛋白质产生电脉冲，使生物体能够移动。进一步的研究表明，当这种称为通道视紫红质的蛋白质暴露在光下时，它会像孔一样打开，允许带正电的离子流入细胞，产生电脉冲。 “他们刚刚发现了神经科学家梦寐以求的转变，”埃尔马尼拉说。

paras.en: Building on the Hegemann and Nagel’s work, Deisseroth began testing whether channelrhodopsin could be used to activate brain cells. He and his colleagues first inserted the gene for channelrhodopsin into cultures of rat nerve cells and found that the cells reacted to light instantaneously. They then introduced the gene into nerve cells in the brains of living mice, along with optical fibers fed through the rodents’ skulls. By beaming blue light through the fibers, the researchers were able to control the movements of the rodents’ whiskers. This technology gave researchers the ability to test the links between certain brain circuits and behaviors.
paras.zh: 在 Hegemann 和 Nagel 的工作基础上，Deisseroth 开始测试视紫红质通道蛋白是否可用于激活脑细胞。他和他的同事首先将视紫红质通道蛋白基因插入大鼠神经细胞培养物中，发现细胞对光立即做出反应。然后，他们将该基因引入活体小鼠大脑的神经细胞中，同时将光纤引入啮齿类动物的头骨中。通过通过纤维发射蓝光，研究人员能够控制啮齿动物胡须的运动。这项技术使研究人员能够测试某些大脑回路和行为之间的联系。

paras.en: “The technology, which soon became known as optogenetics, transformed neuroscience,” El Manira said. In addition to exposing the inner workings of healthy brains, he noted, “it has also helped reveal how brain circuits are disrupted, with implications for conditions such as blindness, depression and dementia.”
paras.zh: “这项技术很快被称为光遗传学，它改变了神经科学，”埃尔马尼拉说。他指出，除了揭示健康大脑的内部运作之外，“它还有助于揭示大脑回路如何被破坏，从而对失明、抑郁和痴呆等疾病产生影响。”

paras.en: For example, the technology has been used improve vision in some patients with retinitis pigmentosa, a disease that degrades light-sensing cells in the retina. It’s also helping researchers investigate the role that a person’s heart plays in how they experience and interact with their surroundings.
paras.zh: 例如，该技术已被用于改善一些患有色素性视网膜炎的患者的视力，这种疾病会降低视网膜中的光敏细胞的功能。它还帮助研究人员调查一个人的心脏在他们如何体验和与周围环境互动中所扮演的角色。

paras.en: At the South Pole, there exists a block of ice unlike any other on Earth. Buried deep beneath the surface of the Antarctic ice sheet, a cubic kilometer of ice is threaded with thousands of beadlike sensors. Known as the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, this immense instrument enables researchers to detect the most elusive particle in the universe — the neutrino.
paras.zh: 在南极，有一块与地球上其他地方不同的冰块。深埋在南极冰盖表面下方，一立方公里的冰上布满了数千个珠状传感器。这个巨大的仪器被称为冰立方中微子观测站，使研究人员能够探测宇宙中最难以捉摸的粒子——中微子。

paras.en: Detecting neutrinos from beyond our solar system had been a goal of scientists for decades, as that could help understand where and how the universe accelerates particles to extraordinary energies.
paras.zh: 几十年来，探测太阳系以外的中微子一直是科学家的目标，因为这可以帮助了解宇宙在何处以及如何将粒子加速到非凡的能量。

paras.en: The researcher who led the creation of the Antarctic observatory, physicist Francis Halzen of the University of Wisconsin–Madison, received this year’s Nobel Prize in physics. Halzen was awarded “for his decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin,” Mark Pearce, a physicist and chair of the Nobel committee for physics, during the Oct. 6 announcement by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.
paras.zh: 领导创建南极天文台的研究人员、威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校的物理学家弗朗西斯·哈尔岑获得了今年的诺贝尔物理学奖。瑞典皇家科学院在 10 月 6 日宣布，诺贝尔物理学委员会主席、物理学家马克·皮尔斯 (Mark Pearce) 授予哈尔岑奖，以表彰他“对冰立方中微子观测站和发现天体物理起源的高能中微子做出的决定性贡献”。

paras.en: Neutrinos are subatomic particles that are chargeless, incredibly small and so ethereal that they often pass through objects without interacting. In fact, billions of neutrinos pass through each of us every second, most of which are formed by nuclear fusion reactions in the sun. But some of these ghostly particles were thought to have originated much farther away, in high-energy particle collisions so distant as to lie beyond the limits of observations. Because neutrinos are not deflected by magnetic fields and rarely interact with matter, the detection of a high-energy neutrino’s trajectory could enable the identification of its distant source. An instrument capable of that task could therefore open a new window into the cosmos.
paras.zh: 中微子是亚原子粒子，不带电荷，非常小，而且如此飘逸，以至于它们经常穿过物体而不发生相互作用。事实上，每秒有数十亿个中微子穿过我们每个人，其中大部分是由太阳的核聚变反应形成的。但其中一些幽灵般的粒子被认为起源于更远的地方，是在高能粒子碰撞中产生的，距离如此之远，超出了观测的范围。由于中微子不会被磁场偏转，并且很少与物质相互作用，因此检测高能中微子的轨迹可以识别其遥远的来源。因此，能够完成这项任务的仪器可以打开一扇通向宇宙的新窗口。

paras.en: In the 1980s, Halzen realized that the South Pole was an ideal location for detecting the rare flashes of light that are generated when neutrinos collide with atomic nuclei. Ice deep inside the Antarctic ice sheet presented a large, transparent medium plunged in darkness, in a spot free from earthquakes and biological interference. It was the perfect stage for a neutrino lightshow.
paras.zh: 20 世纪 80 年代，哈尔岑意识到南极是探测中微子与原子核碰撞时产生的罕见闪光的理想地点。南极冰盖深处的冰呈现出一个巨大的、透明的介质，沉浸在黑暗中，没有地震和生物干扰。这是中微子灯光秀的完美舞台。

paras.en: Halzen’s vision was realized in 2011, when IceCube completed construction. “The biggest risk we took is that nobody knew whether a kilometer-field detector was actually large enough to discover neutrinos beyond our atmosphere from the universe,” Halzen said in a phone call during the announcement ceremony. “It only took us two years to detect them.”
paras.zh: Halzen 的愿景于 2011 年实现，当时 IceCube 竣工。哈尔岑在宣布仪式上的电话中说：“我们冒的最大风险是，没有人知道千米级探测器是否真的足够大，足以发现宇宙大气层之外的中微子。” “我们只花了两年时间就发现了它们。”

paras.en: And the discoveries didn’t end there. In 2018, researchers using IceCube data reported that they had traced a neutrino back to the brilliant core of a distant galaxy, called a blazar, thereby identifying a source for the energetic particles for the first time. And in 2023, researchers used a decade of IceCube data to produce the first map of the Milky Way using anything besides light, simultaneously reporting the first evidence of high-energy neutrinos hailing from within the galaxy.
paras.zh: 发现并没有就此结束。 2018 年，研究人员使用 IceCube 数据报告称，他们已经将中微子追溯到遥远星系（称为耀变体）的明亮核心，从而首次确定了高能粒子的来源。 2023 年，研究人员利用十年来的 IceCube 数据绘制了第一张银河系地图，同时还报告了来自银河系内部高能中微子的第一个证据。

paras.en: Plans for a global network of neutrino detectors are now in motion. So scientists will soon be even better equipped to pinpoint and demystify the distant cosmic accelerators that launch the mysterious particles across the vast reaches of space.
paras.zh: 全球中微子探测器网络的计划现已启动。因此，科学家们很快就会有更好的装备来精确定位和揭开遥远宇宙加速器的神秘面纱，这些加速器在广阔的太空中发射神秘粒子。

paras.en: In nature, the building blocks of life exhibit a striking pattern. Many can exist in two versions that are mirrored images of one another, much like your right and left hand. Such molecules are said to be chiral. However, they overwhelmingly occur as just one of these chiral forms — for instance, amino acids are nearly always left-handed.
paras.zh: 在自然界中，生命的组成部分表现出惊人的模式。许多可以存在两个版本，彼此互为镜像，就像你的右手和左手一样。此类分子被认为是手性的。然而，它们绝大多数只是作为这些手性形式之一出现——例如，氨基酸几乎总是左旋的。

paras.en: This uniformity, known as homochirality, had long puzzled scientists. When chemists first attempted to produce chiral molecules in the lab, they ended up with even proportions of right- and left-handed molecules, or enantiomers.
paras.zh: 这种一致性被称为同手性，长期以来一直困扰着科学家。当化学家第一次尝试在实验室中生产手性分子时，他们最终得到了均匀比例的右旋分子和左旋分子或对映体。

paras.en: “It is this puzzle that this year’s laureates have solved,” Heiner Linke, chair of the Nobel Committee for Chemistry said during the Oct. 7 Nobel Prize in chemistry announcement by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.
paras.zh: “今年的获奖者已经解决了这个难题，”诺贝尔化学委员会主席海纳·林克在瑞典皇家科学院于 10 月 7 日宣布诺贝尔化学奖时说道。

paras.en: Henri Kagan, of the Université Paris-Saclay, and Kenso Soai, of the Tokyo University of Science, split the prize for discoveries leading “to a chemical reaction that spontaneously, without the involvement of other chiral molecules, creates only one mirror image,” said Linke, a physicist at Lund University in Sweden. “This is the first time this had happened since the processes that led to the chirality of life billions of years ago.”
paras.zh: 瑞典隆德大学的物理学家林克说，巴黎萨克雷大学的亨利·卡根和东京理科大学的 Kenso Soai 平分了“一种化学反应的发现，这种化学反应在没有其他手性分子参与的情况下自发地只产生一个镜像”。 “自数十亿年前导致生命手性的过程以来，这是第一次发生这种情况。”

paras.en: Putting aside the laureates’ impact on one of organic chemistry’s greatest mysteries, their research has immensely benefitted the development of pharmaceuticals. So many active drug molecules are chiral, and one enantiomer of a drug might have the desired therapeutic effect while its other might have no effect or even be harmful, Linke said.
paras.zh: 抛开获奖者对有机化学最大谜团之一的影响不谈，他们的研究极大地有益于药物的开发。 Linke说，许多活性药物分子都是手性的，药物的一种对映体可能具有所需的治疗效果，而另一种对映体可能没有效果甚至有害。

paras.en: A notorious example of such harm occurred in the 1950s, when thousands of babies with severe birth defects were born to women who had taken a sedative called thalidomide. It was later revealed that one of thalidomide’s enantiomers was the source of the birth defects. Even making the drug with only the “safe” orientation didn’t solve the problem: It could switch handedness in the body.
paras.zh: 这种伤害的一个臭名昭著的例子发生在 20 世纪 50 年代，当时服用沙利度胺镇静剂的妇女生下了数千名患有严重先天缺陷的婴儿。后来发现，沙利度胺的一种对映体是出生缺陷的根源。即使仅以“安全”方向制造药物也无法解决问题：它可以改变体内的利手习惯。

paras.en: In 1986, Kagan and his colleagues became the first to report chemical reactions that produced specific enantiomers in proportions far exceeding what chemists previously assumed was possible using catalysts.
paras.zh: 1986 年，卡根和他的同事成为第一个报告产生特定对映异构体的化学反应的人，其比例远远超过化学家之前假设的使用催化剂的可能性。

paras.en: Nine years later, Soai and his colleagues reported that they had figured out how to make a chiral catalyst that could, in turn, be used to form itself. That allowed them to perform reactions that resulted in products made almost entirely of one enantiomer. “This is not the final answer,” Soai said of his groundbreaking work on chirality, while calling into the ceremony from Japan. Speaking to future generations, he said “the study of chirality should be more and more developed.”
paras.zh: 九年后，索艾和他的同事报告说，他们已经找到了制造手性催化剂的方法，而这种催化剂又可以用来形成自身。这使得他们能够进行反应，产生几乎完全由一种对映体制成的产品。 “这不是最终的答案，”Soai 在日本参加仪式时谈到他在手性方面的开创性工作。他对后代说：“手性研究应该越来越发展。”

paras.en: Even so, as Nobel committee member Peter Somfai, a chemist at Lund University in Sweden, said during the ceremony: “This is probably the coolest experiment in organic chemistry.”
paras.zh: 即便如此，正如诺贝尔委员会成员、瑞典隆德大学化学家 Peter Somfai 在颁奖典礼上所说：“这可能是有机化学领域最酷的实验。”

articles.title: How the Grand Canyon could have lost 1 billion years of geologic history
articles.author: Lucas Van Wyk Joel

paras.en: In the Grand Canyon, rock layers preserve a relatively continuous record of Earth’s geologic history going back about 2 billion years. But between 520 million and 1.8 billion years, the record is noticeably empty. It’s as if someone broke into a museum and made off with almost an entire wing’s worth of rocks, and sorting out “whodunnit” is one of the coldest cases in all geology.
paras.zh: 在大峡谷中，岩层保存着相对连续的地球地质历史记录，可以追溯到大约 20 亿年前。但在 5.2 亿年到 18 亿年之间，记录明显是空的。这就好像有人闯入博物馆并偷走了几乎整个展馆的岩石，而整理“侦探小说”是所有地质学中最冷的案例之一。

paras.en: Now, scientists studying the Grand Canyon’s rocks say that a gigantic Earth-spanning cliff —with a global glaciation as its accomplice — could be to blame for the heist.
paras.zh: 现在，研究大峡谷岩石的科学家表示，一个横跨地球的巨大悬崖——全球冰川作用是其同谋——可能是这次盗窃事件的罪魁祸首。

paras.en: The giant cliff started forming about 800 million years ago as an ancient supercontinent called Rodinia split apart, Thomas Gernon, an earth scientist at the University of Southampton in England, and colleagues report August 17 in Geology. Forces like rain and ice weathered and eroded the rock and, like waves at the beach steadily erasing one layer of sand after another, deleted a billion years of Earth’s history.
paras.zh: 英国南安普顿大学地球科学家 Thomas Gernon 及其同事于 8 月 17 日在《地质学》杂志上报道称，大约 8 亿年前，当一块名为罗迪尼亚 (Rodinia) 的古老超级大陆分裂时，巨大的悬崖开始形成。雨水和冰等力量风化并侵蚀了岩石，就像海滩上的海浪不断地抹去一层又一层的沙子一样，抹去了地球十亿年的历史。

paras.en: The group used computer models to simulate how ancient Earth evolved over hundreds of millions of years. They watched as the cliff — known as an escarpment — formed around the time in Earth’s history when rocks in the region vanished.
paras.zh: 该小组使用计算机模型来模拟古代地球数亿年的演化过程。他们目睹了悬崖——被称为悬崖——是在地球历史上该地区岩石消失的那段时间形成的。

paras.en: The escarpment most likely extended across much of a continent called Laurentia, the ancient precursor to North America. It stretched from what was to become Alaska all the way to Arizona and would have been about one to two kilometers high.
paras.zh: 悬崖很可能横跨劳伦西亚大陆的大部分地区，劳伦西亚大陆是北美的古代前身。它从后来的阿拉斯加一直延伸到亚利桑那州，高约一到两公里。

paras.en: Some 65 million years ago, the Great Escarpment of Laurentia would have stretched across much of North America, including the spot that would one day become the Grand Canyon and the site of an enduring geologic mystery. The escarpment itself is thought to have formed around 800 million years ago.
paras.zh: 大约 6500 万年前，劳伦西亚大悬崖横跨北美大部分地区，其中包括有一天成为大峡谷的地方和一个持久的地质谜团所在。据认为，悬崖本身形成于大约 8 亿年前。

paras.en: “No study has previously suggested the existence of a continental-scale escarpment in the Grand Canyon region. Our study shows it’s a plausible, straightforward explanation for the immense erosion that took place in the Grand Canyon,” Gernon says. Such an immense cliff created steep slopes that were ideal places for the elements to loosen and make off with exposed rock.
paras.zh: “之前没有研究表明大峡谷地区存在大陆级悬崖。我们的研究表明，这是对大峡谷发生的巨大侵蚀的一个合理而直接的解释，”格农说。如此巨大的悬崖形成了陡峭的斜坡，是自然元素松动并剥落裸露岩石的理想场所。

paras.en: And the escarpment had a lot of help when it came to its disappearing act: ice, lots and lots of ice. The theft of the rocks coincided with an extreme period of glaciation called Snowball Earth. Massive ice sheets formed and may have extended all the way from the poles to equatorial latitudes. As the ice expanded, it would have eroded great quantities of rock, helping create the gap in the record.
paras.zh: 悬崖在消失过程中得到了很多帮助：冰，很多很多的冰。岩石失窃恰逢被称为“雪球地球”的极端冰川时期。巨大的冰盖形成，并可能从两极一直延伸到赤道纬度。随着冰层的扩张，它会侵蚀大量的岩石，从而造成了记录上的差距。

paras.en: And the escarpment, due to its high elevation, would have created ideal conditions for Snowball Earth glaciers and ice sheets to form. In a separate study published in Science, Gernon and a team explained how an escarpment created by tectonic activity was responsible for the formation of the East Antarctic Ice Sheet starting some 34 million years ago. “The exposed rocky peaks of the escarpment would have acted as glacier factories,” Gernon says.
paras.zh: 由于悬崖海拔较高，为雪球地球冰川和冰盖的形成创造了理想的条件。在《科学》杂志上发表的另一项研究中，Gernon 和他的团队解释了约 3400 万年前由构造活动形成的悬崖如何导致东南极冰盖的形成。 “悬崖上裸露的岩石山峰可以充当冰川工厂，”格农说。

paras.en: It remains unclear, however, whether the erosion that erased the rocks occurred before, during or after the Snowball Earth glaciations. “That’s the real hole that needs filling: pinning down the erosion history in space and time, continent by continent, precisely enough,” Gernon says.
paras.zh: 然而，目前尚不清楚消除岩石的侵蚀是否发生在雪球地球冰川作用之前、期间或之后。格农说：“这才是真正需要填补的漏洞：准确地确定各个大陆在空间和时间上的侵蚀历史。”

paras.en: Linking the disappearance of the rocks to verified events in Earth’s history such as the breakup of Rodinia bolsters the case, says Alan Collins, a geologist at Adelaide University in Australia who was not involved in the new study. Not only that, but Gernon’s team points to modern-day examples where similar erosive processes are at work, including a similar escarpment in Antarctica as well as one in South Africa.
paras.zh: 未参与这项新研究的澳大利亚阿德莱德大学地质学家艾伦·柯林斯 (Alan Collins) 表示，将岩石的消失与地球历史上已证实的事件（例如罗迪尼亚的分裂）联系起来，支持了这一论点。不仅如此，格农的团队还指出了类似侵蚀过程正在发挥作用的现代例子，包括南极洲和南非的类似悬崖。

paras.en: Maybe not quite case closed yet, but “I find this very convincing,” Collins says.
paras.zh: 也许案件尚未完全结束，但“我发现这非常有说服力，”柯林斯说。

articles.title: Massive Wave in The Pacific Was The Most Extreme 'Rogue Wave' on Record
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: In November 2020, a freak wave appeared, lifting a lone buoy off the coast of British Columbia 17.6 meters (58 feet) high.
paras.zh: 2020 年 11 月，出现了一股怪异的海浪，将不列颠哥伦比亚省海岸的一个孤零零的浮标提升了 17.6 米（58 英尺）高。

paras.en: A few years later, the four-story wall of water was confirmed to be the most extreme rogue wave ever recorded.
paras.zh: 几年后，四层楼高的水墙被证实是有史以来最极端的巨浪。

paras.en: Such an extraordinary event is thought to happen only once every 1,300 years.
paras.zh: 这种非同寻常的事件被认为每 1,300 年才会发生一次。

paras.en: And if the buoy hadn't been taken for a ride, we might never have known it had occurred.
paras.zh: 如果浮标没有被带走，我们可能永远不会知道它发生了。

paras.en: For centuries, rogue waves were regarded as mere nautical folklore.
paras.zh: 几个世纪以来，汹涌的海浪仅仅被视为航海民间传说。

paras.en: It wasn't until 1995 that myth became reality. On the first day of the new year, a nearly 26-meter (85-foot) wave struck an oil-drilling platform about 160 kilometers (100 miles) off the coast of Norway.
paras.zh: 直到1995年，神话才成为现实。新年第一天，近 26 米（85 英尺）高的海浪袭击了距挪威海岸约 160 公里（100 英里）的石油钻井平台。

paras.en: At the time, the so-called Draupner wave defied all previous models scientists had put together.
paras.zh: 当时，所谓的德劳普纳波违背了科学家之前建立的所有模型。

paras.en: Since then, dozens more rogue waves have been recorded (some even in lakes), and while the one that surfaced near Ucluelet, Vancouver Island was not the tallest, its relative size compared to the waves around it was unprecedented.
paras.zh: 从那时起，又记录了数十次狂浪（有些甚至在湖泊中），虽然温哥华岛尤克卢利特附近出现的浪不是最高的，但与周围波浪相比，其相对大小是前所未有的。

paras.en: Scientists define a rogue wave as any wave more than twice the height of the waves surrounding it. The Draupner wave, for instance, was 25.6 meters tall, while its neighbors were only 12 meters tall.
paras.zh: 科学家将异常波浪定义为任何高度超过其周围波浪两倍的波浪。例如，Draupner 波高 25.6 米，而它的邻居只有 12 米高。

paras.en: In comparison, the Ucluelet wave was nearly three times the size of its peers.
paras.zh: 相比之下，尤克卢利特波浪的规模几乎是同类波浪的三倍。

paras.en: "Proportionally, the Ucluelet wave is likely the most extreme rogue wave ever recorded," explained physicist Johannes Gemmrich from the University of Victoria in 2022.
paras.zh: 维多利亚大学的物理学家约翰内斯·格姆里奇 (Johannes Gemmrich) 于 2022 年解释说：“按比例来说，尤克卢利特波可能是有史以来最极端的异常波。”

paras.en: "Only a few rogue waves in high sea states have been observed directly, and nothing of this magnitude."
paras.zh: “在公海状态下只直接观察到了一些异常的波浪，而且没有观察到如此大规模的波浪。”

paras.en: Today, researchers are still trying to figure out how rogue waves are formed so we can better predict when they will arise. This includes measuring rogue waves in real time and also running models on the way they get whipped up by the wind.
paras.zh: 今天，研究人员仍在试图弄清楚异常波是如何形成的，以便我们能够更好地预测它们何时出现。这包括实时测量异常波浪，并根据波浪被风吹起的方式运行模型。

paras.en: The buoy that picked up the Ucluelet wave was placed offshore, along with dozens of others, by a research institute called MarineLabs in an attempt to learn more about hazards out in the deep.
paras.zh: 一个名为“海洋实验室”的研究机构将接收尤克卢利特海浪的浮标与其他数十个浮标一起放置在海上，试图了解更多有关深海危险的信息。

paras.en: "The unpredictability of rogue waves, and the sheer power of these 'walls of water' can make them incredibly dangerous to marine operations and the public," said MarineLabs CEO Scott Beatty.
paras.zh: MarineLabs 首席执行官斯科特·比蒂 (Scott Beatty) 表示：“狂暴波浪的不可预测性以及这些‘水墙’的巨大力量可能使它们对海洋作业和公众造成极其危险。”

paras.en: "The potential of predicting rogue waves remains an open question, but our data is helping to better understand when, where, and how rogue waves form, and the risks that they pose."
paras.zh: “预测异常波浪的潜力仍然是一个悬而未决的问题，但我们的数据有助于更好地了解异常波浪形成的时间、地点和方式，以及它们带来的风险。”

paras.en: Even when freak waves occur far offshore, they can still destroy marine operations, wind farms, or oil rigs. If they are big enough, they can even put the lives of beachgoers at risk.
paras.zh: 即使异常波浪发生在离岸很远的地方，它们仍然可以摧毁海上作业、风电场或石油钻井平台。如果它们足够大，甚至可以危及海滩游客的生命。

paras.en: Luckily, neither Ucluelet nor Draupner caused any severe damage or took any lives, but other rogue waves have.
paras.zh: 幸运的是，尤克卢利特和德劳普纳都没有造成任何严重破坏或夺走任何人的生命，但其他的狂暴浪潮却造成了这种情况。

paras.en: Some ships that went missing in the 1970s, for instance, are now thought to have been sunk by sudden, looming waves.
paras.zh: 例如，一些在 20 世纪 70 年代失踪的船只现在被认为是被突然逼近的海浪击沉的。

paras.en: The floating wreckage left behind looks like the work of an immense white cap.
paras.zh: 留下的漂浮残骸看起来就像一顶巨大的白色帽子的作品。

paras.en: Unfortunately, a 2020 study predicted that wave heights in the North Pacific will increase with climate change, suggesting the Ucluelet wave may not hold its record for as long as our current predictions suggest.
paras.zh: 不幸的是，2020 年的一项研究预测，北太平洋的波浪高度将随着气候变化而增加，这表明尤克卢利特波浪可能不会像我们目前的预测那样长时间保持其记录。

paras.en: Experimental research published in 2024 suggests these monstrous waves can be up to four times higher than previously thought possible.
paras.zh: 2024 年发表的实验研究表明，这些巨大的波浪可能比之前认为的高出四倍。

paras.en: "We are aiming to improve safety and decision-making for marine operations and coastal communities through widespread measurement of the world's coastlines," said MarineLabs CEO Scott Beatty.
paras.zh: MarineLabs 首席执行官斯科特·比蒂 (Scott Beatty) 表示：“我们的目标是通过广泛测量世界海岸线来提高海洋作业和沿海社区的安全性和决策能力。”

paras.en: "Capturing this once-in-a-millennium wave, right in our backyard, is a thrilling indicator of the power of coastal intelligence to transform marine safety."
paras.zh: “在我们的后院捕捉到这一千年一遇的海浪，是一个令人兴奋的指标，表明沿海情报改变海洋安全的力量。”

paras.en: The effort to predict rogue waves got a boost in February 2026, when a team led by researchers from the University of South Florida published a new analysis in Ocean Science, testing years of real buoy data against the global wave models scientists currently rely on to forecast ocean conditions.
paras.zh: 2026 年 2 月，由南佛罗里达大学研究人员领导的一个团队在《海洋科学》上发表了一项新分析，将多年的真实浮标数据与科学家目前用来预测海洋状况的全球波浪模型进行了测试，从而推动了预测异常波浪的努力。

paras.en: The team found those models consistently underestimate just how extreme waves can get, missing much of the long tail of rare, towering waves that buoys actually pick up in the real world.
paras.zh: 研究小组发现，这些模型始终低估了极端波浪的强度，忽略了现实世界中实际出现的罕见、高耸的波浪的长尾。

paras.en: Rogue waves turned out to be far from random, too.
paras.zh: 事实证明，流氓浪潮也远非随机。

paras.en: They peaked in winter and clustered most heavily off the US West Coast, with the North Atlantic a close second – putting the Pacific Northwest, where the Ucluelet wave struck, squarely in the highest-risk zone.
paras.zh: 它们在冬季达到顶峰，在美国西海岸附近聚集最多，北大西洋紧随其后，使尤克卢利特海浪袭击的太平洋西北地区完全处于风险最高的区域。

paras.en: Related: Scientists Collected Deep-Sea Rocks. They Spontaneously Caught Fire in The Lab.
paras.zh: 相关：科学家收集深海岩石。他们在实验室里自发起火。

paras.en: The researchers also flagged a possible early-warning sign buried in the data.
paras.zh: 研究人员还标记了数据中可能隐藏的预警信号。

paras.en: In roughly three-quarters of the rogue waves they examined, a sharp dip in wave correlation was followed by a rapid rebound right before the wave hit – a pattern they hope could eventually feed into real-time forecasting tools.
paras.zh: 在他们检查的大约四分之三的异常波浪中，波浪相关性急剧下降之后，在波浪袭来之前迅速反弹——他们希望这种模式最终能够纳入实时预测工具中。

paras.en: The study on the Ucluelet wave was published in Scientific Reports.
paras.zh: 关于尤克卢利特波的研究发表在《科学报告》上。

articles.title: An Earth-Sized Planet Could Survive With 2 Suns Just 16 Light-Years Away
articles.author: Ivan Farkas

paras.en: Planets with two suns have intrigued our cosmic imagination ever since they appeared in a popular work of fiction set in a galaxy far, far away.
paras.zh: 自从出现在一部以遥远星系为背景的流行小说中以来，拥有两个太阳的行星就引起了我们的宇宙想象力。

paras.en: That's right, the globally famous King in Yellow, published in 1895. Oh, and Star Wars, of course.
paras.zh: 没错，就是 1895 年出版的全球闻名的《黄衣之王》。哦，当然还有《星球大战》。

paras.en: But can potentially habitable planets actually exist in binary star systems?
paras.zh: 但潜在的宜居行星真的可以存在于双星系统中吗？

paras.en: New research suggests yes, absolutely, and for a very long time – while also squashing hopes for giant planets in the system behind the oldest exoplanet claim ever proposed.
paras.zh: 新的研究表明，是的，绝对的，而且持续了很长一段时间——同时也粉碎了有史以来最古老的系外行星主张背后的系统中存在巨行星的希望。

paras.en: Our Solar System is unusual because it's the only one we know of with robots zipping between its planets.
paras.zh: 我们的太阳系很不寻常，因为它是我们所知道的唯一一个机器人在其行星之间穿行的系统。

paras.en: "Our solar system, with only one star, is actually somewhat unusual. Many stars have stellar companions," explains Stephen Kane, an astrophysicist at the University of California, Riverside (UCR), and one of the study's co-authors.
paras.zh: “我们的太阳系只有一颗恒星，实际上有些不寻常。许多恒星都有伴星，”该研究的合著者之一、加州大学河滨分校 (UCR) 的天体物理学家斯蒂芬·凯恩 (Stephen Kane) 解释道。

paras.en: "You might imagine that second star coming through like a wrecking ball and making it impossible for an Earth-sized planet to survive in the habitable zone. But these simulations show that isn't necessarily the case."
paras.zh: “你可能会想象第二颗恒星像一个破坏球一样穿过，使地球大小的行星无法在宜居带生存。但这些模拟表明情况不一定如此。”

paras.en: An immense astronomy team from more than a dozen institutions focused on the binary system named 70 Ophiuchi (70 Oph AB), whose two stars are K dwarfs that are approximately 88 percent and 73 percent the mass of the Sun and possibly around 3 billion years old, according to the team's calculations.
paras.zh: 来自十几家机构的庞大天文学团队专注于名为 70 Ophiuchi (70 Oph AB) 的双星系统，该双星系统的两颗恒星是 K 矮星，质量约为太阳的 88% 和 73%，根据该团队的计算，其年龄可能约为 30 亿年。

paras.en: The orange-y K dwarfs are one rung down the stellar ladder from our Sun, and therefore smaller, dimmer, and cooler.
paras.zh: 橙色 K 矮星是太阳阶梯上的一级矮星，因此更小、更暗且温度更低。

paras.en: They're prime targets in the search for habitability because they're calmer and less active than red dwarfs and potentially seven times longer-lived than the Sun, with lifespans of up to 70 billion years.
paras.zh: 它们是寻找宜居性的主要目标，因为它们比红矮星更平静、不那么活跃，而且它们的寿命可能是太阳的七倍，寿命可达 700 亿年。

paras.en: 70 Oph AB is particularly attractive because it's in our stellar neighborhood, only about 16 light-years away, or four times farther than our nearest neighbors in the Proxima Centauri system.
paras.zh: 70 Oph AB 特别有吸引力，因为它位于我们的恒星邻居中，距离我们仅约 16 光年，比我们在比邻星系统中最近的邻居远四倍。

paras.en: It has also been known as a binary for nearly 250 years, thanks to William Herschel.
paras.zh: 由于威廉·赫歇尔 (William Herschel)，它也被称为二进制近 250 年。

paras.en: So the team incorporated recent and archival radial velocity (RV) measurements of both stars, including data from eight instruments for the primary star, across a century of observation.
paras.zh: 因此，该团队整合了两颗恒星的最新和档案径向速度 (RV) 测量结果，包括来自主恒星的八台仪器在一个世纪的观测中获得的数据。

paras.en: RV is the second-most successful planet-finding method in our astrophysical arsenal, responsible for over 1,200 exoplanets.
paras.zh: RV 是我们天体物理学库中第二成功的行星寻找方法，已发现 1,200 多颗系外行星。

paras.en: The RV method measures the tiny changes in a star's velocity that result from the gravitational nudge of another celestial body, be it a planet, companion star, or otherwise.
paras.zh: RV 方法测量恒星速度的微小变化，这些变化是由于另一个天体（无论是行星、伴星还是其他天体）的引力推动而产生的。

paras.en: As that star thus draws closer to Earth, its light becomes ever-so-slightly bluer, and then correspondingly redder as it's moving away from us.
paras.zh: 当这颗恒星越来越接近地球时，它的光变得稍微更蓝，然后当它远离我们时相应地更红。

paras.en: Amazingly, the researchers achieved an RV precision of better than 1 meter per second.
paras.zh: 令人惊讶的是，研究人员实现了优于每秒 1 米的 RV 精度。

paras.en: For perspective, that's like taking a leisurely stroll and quickening your pace to overtake a fellow pedestrian, or quickly escape your local donut shop's tempting aromas.
paras.zh: 从角度来看，这就像悠闲地散步并加快步伐以超越其他行人，或者快速逃离当地甜甜圈店的诱人香气。

paras.en: That astronomers can measure this change in the velocity of an entire star, a giant nuclear furnace trillions of miles away, is a testament to science.
paras.zh: 天文学家可以测量整个恒星（数万亿英里外的巨型核炉）速度的变化，这是对科学的证明。

paras.en: The researchers then injected fake planet signals into their treasure trove of data to see what they could detect. They also simulated Earth-mass planets at 2,000 different distances from the primary star, tracking each one over 10 million years.
paras.zh: 然后研究人员将虚假的行星信号注入他们的数据宝库中，看看他们能检测到什么。他们还模拟了距主恒星 2000 个不同距离的地球质量行星，对每一颗行星的跟踪时间超过 1000 万年。

paras.en: "We calculated the boundaries of the habitable zone around the primary star. Then I tested whether an Earth-mass planet could maintain a stable orbit at different distances within that zone," explains Skylar D'Angiolillo, an Earth and planetary sciences researcher at UCR and one of the study's co-authors.
paras.zh: “我们计算了主恒星周围宜居带的边界。然后我测试了一颗地球质量的行星是否可以在该区域内不同距离处保持稳定的轨道，”加州大学河滨分校的地球和行星科学研究人员、该研究的合著者之一斯凯拉·德安吉奥利洛（Skylar D'Angiolillo）解释道。

paras.en: "What we found is that stable orbits are possible in the habitable zone of the primary star. You might expect the second star to disrupt those orbits, but that isn't necessarily what happens."
paras.zh: “我们发现，主恒星的宜居带中可能存在稳定的轨道。你可能会认为第二颗恒星会扰乱这些轨道，但这不一定会发生。”

paras.en: The researchers were also able to rule out the presence of Jupiter-mass-or-larger giant exoplanets around the two stars, going out to about five astronomical units (AU) from the primary star, or about the distance from the Sun at which a Jupiter-mass gas giant exists in our own Solar System (hint: Jupiter).
paras.zh: 研究人员还能够排除这两颗恒星周围存在木星质量或更大的巨型系外行星的可能性，这些行星距离主恒星大约五个天文单位（AU），或者大约是我们太阳系中存在木星质量气态巨行星的距离（提示：木星）。

paras.en: This is intriguing because in 1855, British astronomer William Jacob claimed that 70 Oph AB had a planet, making it the first host of an exoplanet candidate, University of Michigan (U-M) researchers point out.
paras.zh: 密歇根大学 (U-M) 研究人员指出，这很有趣，因为 1855 年，英国天文学家 William Jacob 声称 70 Oph AB 拥有一颗行星，使其成为系外行星候选者的第一颗宿主。

paras.en: Jacob's claim didn't survive scrutiny, but more recent measurements showed a 'wobble' that could still have been explained by a Jupiter-sized planet.
paras.zh: 雅各布的说法没有经受住审查，但最近的测量显示，这种“摆动”仍然可以用木星大小的行星来解释。

paras.en: Instead, this supposed planetary signal appears to have been due to plain old stellar activity, the bane of the RV method.
paras.zh: 相反，这个所谓的行星信号似乎是由普通的古老恒星活动引起的，这是 RV 方法的祸根。

paras.en: "It's a mix of disappointment and excitement," says Yiting Li, an astronomer at U-M and the study's first author.
paras.zh: “这是失望和兴奋的混合体，”密歇根大学天文学家、该研究的第一作者李一婷说。

paras.en: "We're finding out that there isn't a Jupiter-sized planet, but we're also opening the latest chapter on this historic system."
paras.zh: “我们发现不存在木星大小的行星，但我们也揭开了这个历史系统的最新篇章。”

paras.en: However, terrestrial planets remain below the detection threshold.
paras.zh: 然而，类地行星仍然低于探测阈值。

paras.en: So, importantly, this suggests that Earth-mass planets could still exist here, as the researchers modeled where they're most likely to be found and to be stable – providing a framework that can be used for other binaries as well.
paras.zh: 因此，重要的是，这表明地球质量的行星仍然可能存在于此，因为研究人员模拟了它们最有可能被发现并稳定的地方——提供了一个也可用于其他双星的框架。

paras.en: And, according to NASA, "More than half of all stars in the sky have one or more partners," so this can significantly expand our future exploration efforts.
paras.zh: 而且，根据美国宇航局的说法，“天空中一半以上的恒星都有一个或多个合作伙伴”，因此这可以显着扩大我们未来的探索工作。

paras.en: Especially when next-(next)-generation observations come online, such as NASA's promising Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), designed to specifically explore and directly image alien worlds.
paras.zh: 尤其是当下一代观测上线时，例如美国宇航局前景光明的宜居世界天文台（HWO），其设计目的是专门探索和直接成像外星世界。

paras.en: "Overall, our results demonstrate that it is possible for the 70 Oph system to host planets on S-type orbits around the primary star, including terrestrial planets on stable orbits within the [habitable zone] region," the researchers conclude.
paras.zh: 研究人员总结道：“总的来说，我们的结果表明，70 Oph 系统有可能在主恒星周围的 S 型轨道上容纳行星，包括在[宜居带]区域内稳定轨道上的类地行星。”

paras.en: "If stellar binaries can host Earth-like planets, 70 Oph is one of the best places to look."
paras.zh: “如果双星系统可以容纳类地行星，那么 70 Oph 是最好的观测地点之一。”

paras.en: The research has been published in The Astrophysical Journal.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《天体物理学杂志》上。

articles.title: Lifting Weights Changes Your Fat Long Before You Lose Weight – at Least in Mice
articles.author: David Nield

paras.en: A lot of biological changes happen in the body once someone starts losing weight.
paras.zh: 一旦有人开始减肥，体内就会发生很多生物学变化。

paras.en: For researchers looking at the impact of diet, exercise, or any other factor, it can be difficult to untangle these weight loss effects from whatever it is they're trying to measure.
paras.zh: 对于研究饮食、运动或任何其他因素影响的研究人员来说，可能很难将这些减肥效果与他们试图测量的任何东西区分开来。

paras.en: To get some clarity on the effects of strength training on fat cells before weight loss kicks in, researchers from the University of Campinas in Brazil ran experiments with obese mice over the course of a week.
paras.zh: 为了弄清楚减肥开始前力量训练对脂肪细胞的影响，巴西坎皮纳斯大学的研究人员对肥胖小鼠进行了为期一周的实验。

paras.en: They studied the visceral fat around the organs before the animals had started to shed the pounds.
paras.zh: 在动物开始减肥之前，他们研究了器官周围的内脏脂肪。

paras.en: Compared to sedentary obese mice, the mice on the strength training regimen had less fat around their intestines and smaller fat cells (which typically indicates healthier fat tissue).
paras.zh: 与久坐的肥胖小鼠相比，接受力量训练的小鼠肠道周围脂肪较少，脂肪细胞较小（这通常表明脂肪组织更健康）。

paras.en: There were also signs of positive changes in fat storage and fat breakdown signals.
paras.zh: 脂肪储存和脂肪分解信号也出现了积极变化的迹象。

paras.en: The study results, published in Life Sciences, suggest that strength training improves metabolic health before any associated weight loss – though the findings still need to be replicated in human trials.
paras.zh: 发表在《生命科学》杂志上的研究结果表明，力量训练可以在任何相关的减肥之前改善代谢健康，尽管这些发现仍需要在人体试验中得到重复。

paras.en: "People tend to think that if they've been strength training for two months and haven't lost weight, it hasn't done any good," says physician Leandro Moura.
paras.zh: “人们往往认为，如果他们进行了两个月的力量训练却没有减轻体重，那就没有任何效果，”医生莱安德罗·莫拉 (Leandro Moura) 说。

paras.en: "But what we saw in this study is that after just seven days of strength training – even when there was still no weight loss – the molecular pathways that promote fat accumulation were less active, while those that stimulate fat breakdown were more active."
paras.zh: “但我们在这项研究中看到的是，经过仅仅 7 天的力量训练——即使体重仍然没有减轻——促进脂肪积累的分子途径变得不那么活跃，而那些刺激脂肪分解的分子途径则更加活跃。”

paras.en: To simulate the effects of weight training on the study animals, the researchers directed the obese mice to climb a 70-centimeter (27.6-inch) staircase with a weight attached to their tails. Sessions included 20 climbs, with rest periods of 60–90 seconds, at 70 percent of the maximum capacity of the rodents, and there were seven sessions in all.
paras.zh: 为了模拟重量训练对研究动物的影响，研究人员引导肥胖小鼠爬上 70 厘米（27.6 英寸）的楼梯，并在其尾巴上附有重物。训练包括 20 次攀爬，休息时间为 60-90 秒，啮齿动物的最大能力为 70%，总共有 7 次训练。

paras.en: "We calculated how much weight each mouse could carry while climbing a staircase," says Moura.
paras.zh: “我们计算了每只老鼠爬楼梯时可以承受的重量，”莫拉说。

paras.en: "Obviously, it isn't possible to replicate the exact strength training exercises performed by a person, but we were able to induce a similar effort in the body, with more intense contractions, effectively mimicking a strength training session for humans."
paras.zh: “显然，不可能精确地复制一个人进行的力量训练练习，但我们能够在身体中引起类似的努力，通过更强烈的收缩，有效地模仿人类的力量训练课程。”

paras.en: Fat tissue samples from these strength training mice were then compared with tissue from obese mice who hadn't done any exercise.
paras.zh: 然后将这些力量训练小鼠的脂肪组织样本与未进行任何运动的肥胖小鼠的组织进行比较。

paras.en: As well as the benefits mentioned above, the team also looked at two proteins, ABHD5 and ATGL. ABHD5 is one of the drivers for breaking down fats: It was at a reduced level in the obese, sedentary mice, but in the strength training group, ABHD5 levels were normal – and interactions with ATGL, a fat-dismantling enzyme, increased too.
paras.zh: 除了上述优点外，该团队还研究了两种蛋白质：ABHD5 和 ATGL。 ABHD5 是分解脂肪的驱动因素之一：在肥胖、久坐的小鼠中，ABHD5 水平降低，但在力量训练组中，ABHD5 水平正常，并且与 ATGL（一种脂肪分解酶）的相互作用也增加。

paras.en: Add in a dialing down of the Scd1 gene in the exercised mice – which is involved in producing fat – and the researchers say there's evidence that strength training can work alongside aerobic exercise for reducing weight.
paras.zh: 再加上运动小鼠中与脂肪生成有关的 Scd1 基因的下调，研究人员表示，有证据表明力量训练可以与有氧运动一起发挥减肥作用。

paras.en: "Both types of exercise activate similar pathways – at different intensities – as well as different pathways," says Moura.
paras.zh: “两种类型的运动都会激活相似的途径（强度不同）以及不同的途径，”莫拉说。

paras.en: "Therefore, combining the two remains the best recommendation and the best strategy for those who want to lose weight."
paras.zh: “因此，对于那些想要减肥的人来说，将两者结合起来仍然是最好的建议和最好的策略。”

paras.en: The next steps, besides working towards the long-term goal of clinical trials, are to look at the longer-term effects of strength training in mice, and to assess how the impacts might vary when it comes to different types of fat, in different places in the body.
paras.zh: 除了努力实现临床试验的长期目标之外，接下来的步骤是研究小鼠力量训练的长期影响，并评估当涉及到身体不同部位的不同类型的脂肪时，影响可能会如何变化。

paras.en: That exercise is good for the body has been established for a long time – but by filling in some of the details, researchers can figure out which types of exercise are best for which people, and how they can be optimized.
paras.zh: 锻炼对身体有益这一说法由来已久，但通过填写一些细节，研究人员可以找出哪些类型的锻炼最适合哪些人，以及如何优化它们。

paras.en: "We've always heard that physical exercise burns fat and helps you lose weight, but we rarely stop to think about how that happens, how much exercise is needed, and what that fat burning actually means," says Moura.
paras.zh: “我们一直听说体育锻炼可以燃烧脂肪并帮助减肥，但我们很少停下来思考这是如何发生的，需要多少运动，以及脂肪燃烧实际上意味着什么，”莫拉说。

paras.en: The research has been published in Life Sciences.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《生命科学》杂志上。

articles.title: MIT astronomers catch a star in a feast that could last billions of years

paras.en: MIT astronomers catch a star in a feast that could last billions of years
paras.zh: 麻省理工学院的天文学家在一场可能持续数十亿年的盛宴中捕获了一颗恒星

paras.en: Scientists discovered a star slowly eating its brown dwarf companion in a cosmic feast that could last billions of years.
paras.zh: 科学家们发现，一颗恒星在一场可能持续数十亿年的宇宙盛宴中慢慢地吞噬着它的褐矮星同伴。

paras.en: - Astronomers have discovered a bizarre star system about 300 light-years from Earth where a small star is slowly devouring a nearby brown dwarf, an object too massive to be a planet but too small to be a true star. Unlike stars that rapidly swallow their companions, this one is gradually stealing material in a process that could continue for billions of years.
paras.zh: - 天文学家发现了一个距地球约 300 光年的奇异恒星系统，其中一颗小恒星正在慢慢吞噬附近的一颗褐矮星，褐矮星的质量太大，无法成为行星，但又太小，无法成为真正的恒星。与迅速吞噬同伴的恒星不同，这颗恒星正在逐渐窃取物质，这一过程可能会持续数十亿年。

paras.en: Astronomers have discovered an unusual star system about 300 light-years from Earth where a small star is gradually consuming a nearby brown dwarf. Instead of swallowing its companion in one dramatic event, the star is steadily pulling material from it, creating a cosmic feeding process that could continue for billions of years.
paras.zh: 天文学家在距离地球约 300 光年的地方发现了一个不寻常的恒星系统，其中一颗小恒星正在逐渐吞噬附近的一颗褐矮星。这颗恒星并没有在一场戏剧性的事件中吞噬它的同伴，而是不断地从中吸取物质，创造了一个可能持续数十亿年的宇宙进食过程。

paras.en: Most planets, including Earth, travel around their stars in relatively stable orbits. But these peaceful arrangements can sometimes end violently. If a planet ventures too close to its host star, the star's gravity can drag it inward and eventually engulf it.
paras.zh: 大多数行星，包括地球，都在相对稳定的轨道上绕恒星运行。但这些和平安排有时可能会以暴力结束。如果一颗行星过于靠近其主恒星，恒星的引力就会将其向内拖拽并最终将其吞没。

paras.en: Scientists have observed many planetary systems with stable orbits, along with a small number of stars caught rapidly swallowing their planetary companions. Now, researchers have identified something that falls between those two extremes.
paras.zh: 科学家们观察到许多具有稳定轨道的行星系统，以及少数被快速吞噬其行星同伴的恒星。现在，研究人员发现了介于这两个极端之间的东西。

paras.en: In a study published October 5 in Nature Astronomy, an international team led by scientists at MIT describes a star that is slowly feeding on a brown dwarf, an object more massive than a typical planet but not massive enough to sustain the hydrogen fusion that powers ordinary stars.
paras.zh: 在 10 月 5 日发表在《自然天文学》上的一项研究中，由麻省理工学院科学家领导的一个国际团队描述了一颗恒星正在缓慢地以褐矮星为食，褐矮星是一种比典型行星更大的物体，但质量不足以维持为普通恒星提供动力的氢聚变。

paras.en: The system, designated ZTF J0440+2325, lies within our Milky Way galaxy approximately 300 light-years away. It is the first observed example of a low-mass star steadily drawing material from another low-mass object.
paras.zh: 该系统被命名为 ZTF J0440+2325，位于我们的银河系内，距离我们大约 300 光年。这是第一个观察到的低质量恒星从另一个低质量天体稳定吸取物质的例子。

paras.en: Even more remarkably, the transfer of material appears to be happening so slowly that the star could continue feeding on its companion for hundreds of thousands of years, potentially even billions.
paras.zh: 更值得注意的是，物质的转移似乎发生得如此缓慢，以至于恒星可以继续以其伴星为食数十万年，甚至可能数十亿年。

paras.en: "When we think of stars interacting with planets or brown dwarfs, the picture is always that the star eventually swallows the other thing," says Kevin Burdge, assistant professor of physics at MIT. "This is what will happen to the Earth when the sun becomes a red giant. But here, we've found an alternative: Instead of swallowing the thing up, the star can gradually eat it, for billions of years."
paras.zh: 麻省理工学院物理学助理教授凯文·伯奇（Kevin Burdge）说：“当我们想到恒星与行星或棕矮星相互作用时，我们总是会想到恒星最终会吞掉其他东西。” “这就是当太阳变成红巨星时地球将会发生的事情。但在这里，我们找到了另一种选择：恒星可以在数十亿年的时间里逐渐吞噬它，而不是吞噬它。”

paras.en: The MIT research team also includes Aaron Householder, Kaitlyn Shin, Saul Rappaport, Joheen Chakraborty, and Emma Chickles. Additional collaborators contributed from Caltech, the University of Hawaii, the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias and Universidad de La Laguna in Spain, and the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics.
paras.zh: 麻省理工学院的研究团队还包括 Aaron Householder、Kaitlyn Shin、Saul Rappaport、Joheen Chakraborty 和 Emma Chickles。其他合作者来自加州理工学院、夏威夷大学、加那利天文研究所和西班牙拉古纳大学，以及哈佛-史密森天体物理学中心。

paras.en: A Mysterious Signal That Puzzled Astronomers for Years
paras.zh: 多年来困扰天文学家的神秘信号

paras.en: The first clue to this unusual stellar relationship came from the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF), an astronomical survey that searches for objects whose brightness changes over time.
paras.zh: 这种不寻常的恒星关系的第一个线索来自兹威基瞬态设施（ZTF），这是一项天文调查，旨在寻找亮度随时间变化的物体。

paras.en: Operating with a telescope at Palomar Observatory in California, ZTF repeatedly photographs large sections of the night sky. Its sensitive camera can detect sudden or unusual changes in light that may indicate powerful cosmic events, including exploding stars called supernovae, gamma-ray bursts, and collisions between neutron stars.
paras.zh: ZTF 使用加州帕洛玛天文台的望远镜反复拍摄大片夜空。其灵敏的相机可以检测到突然或不寻常的光线变化，这些变化可能预示着强大的宇宙事件，包括称为超新星的恒星爆炸、伽马射线暴以及中子星之间的碰撞。

paras.en: Several years ago, while examining observations collected by ZTF, Burdge noticed a particularly strange pattern.
paras.zh: 几年前，在检查 ZTF 收集的观测结果时，伯奇注意到一个特别奇怪的模式。

paras.en: Astronomers study changes in an object's brightness using a graph called a light curve. For some supernovae, these graphs form a rounded, bell-like shape as the exploding star grows brighter and then gradually fades.
paras.zh: 天文学家使用称为光曲线的图表来研究物体亮度的变化。对于某些超新星，随着爆炸的恒星变得更亮，然后逐渐变暗，这些图形会形成圆形的钟状形状。

paras.en: The signal Burdge encountered looked completely different. Instead of a smooth rise and fall, the brightness repeatedly traced something resembling a triangle.
paras.zh: 伯奇遇到的信号看起来完全不同。亮度不是平滑地上升和下降，而是重复地描绘出类似三角形的东西。

paras.en: "I remember first looking at this and thinking, stars don't make triangular waveforms like this," he recalls.
paras.zh: “我记得第一次看到这个并想，恒星不会产生这样的三角波形，”他回忆道。

paras.en: At the time, Burdge and his colleagues were investigating another unusual signal that turned out to originate from a system known as a "black widow binary."
paras.zh: 当时，伯奇和他的同事正在调查另一个不寻常的信号，结果证明该信号源自一个被称为“黑寡妇二进制”的系统。

paras.en: These systems contain a neutron star, the extraordinarily dense remnant of a massive star, that spins rapidly while stripping material from a much smaller companion. They are named after black widow spiders because of the way the neutron star gradually destroys its partner.
paras.zh: 这些系统包含一颗中子星，这是一颗大质量恒星的极其致密的残余物，它快速旋转，同时从一个小得多的伴星中剥离物质。它们以黑寡妇蜘蛛命名，因为中子星逐渐摧毁其伙伴的方式。

paras.en: Burdge initially considered whether the repeating triangular signal might come from another black widow system. However, the observations did not match what astronomers normally expect.
paras.zh: 伯奇最初考虑重复的三角信号是否可能来自另一个黑寡妇系统。然而，观测结果与天文学家的通常预期不符。

paras.en: In a typical black widow binary, the strong contrast between the masses of the two objects produces a distinctive motion. The smaller companion moves rapidly around the much heavier neutron star, creating detectable changes in the light reaching Earth.
paras.zh: 在典型的黑寡妇双星中，两个物体质量之间的强烈对比产生了独特的运动。较小的伴星围绕较重的中子星快速移动，在到达地球的光线中产生可检测到的变化。

paras.en: But the mysterious triangular signal showed no evidence of the same pronounced motion.
paras.zh: 但神秘的三角形信号没有显示出相同明显运动的证据。

paras.en: "We weren't seeing that whipping back and forth here," Burdge says. "It didn't make any sense. We couldn't explain what this was."
paras.zh: “我们在这里没有看到这种来回鞭打的情况，”伯奇说。 “这没有任何意义。我们无法解释这是什么。”

paras.en: That discrepancy led the researchers to consider another possibility. Perhaps the system did not contain one extremely massive object paired with a much lighter companion. Instead, both objects might have relatively small masses, allowing them to orbit each other with much less dramatic motion.
paras.zh: 这种差异促使研究人员考虑另一种可能性。也许该系统并不包含一个质量极大的物体和一个重量轻得多的伴星。相反，这两个物体可能具有相对较小的质量，从而使它们能够以不那么剧烈的运动绕彼此运行。

paras.en: "If you have less mass in the system overall, things can gently orbit each other without whipping back and forth," Burdge says. "That was the idea. But we never had any proof. And this weird triangle just sat for years."
paras.zh: 伯奇说：“如果整个系统的质量较小，物体就可以轻轻地彼此绕轨道运行，而不会来回摆动。” “这就是想法。但我们从来没有任何证据。这个奇怪的三角形已经存在了很多年。”

paras.en: A Brown Dwarf That Orbits Its Star Every 87 Minutes
paras.zh: 每 87 分钟绕恒星一周的褐矮星

paras.en: Eventually, Burdge and Aaron Householder, a graduate student in MIT's Department of Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences, returned to the unexplained signal.
paras.zh: 最终，伯奇和麻省理工学院地球、大气和行星科学系的研究生亚伦·豪斯霍尔德（Aaron Householder）回到了这个无法解释的信号。

paras.en: Using the original ZTF observations, they identified its source as an object roughly 300 light-years away in the Milky Way. They then directed several telescopes toward the system, ZTF J0440+2325, to investigate its properties in greater detail.
paras.zh: 利用最初的 ZTF 观测结果，他们确定其来源是银河系中距离大约 300 光年的一个物体。然后，他们将几台望远镜对准了该系统 ZTF J0440+2325，以更详细地研究其特性。

paras.en: A key measurement involved determining how much the system's objects move in response to their mutual gravitational attraction. Although the researchers detected some wobbling, it was far smaller than the motion typically associated with black widow binaries.
paras.zh: 一个关键的测量涉及确定系统物体响应其相互引力而移动的程度。尽管研究人员检测到了一些摆动，但它远小于通常与黑寡妇双星相关的运动。

paras.en: "That was the real clincher for this system," Householder says. "When we measured that wobble, we found we were not seeing a black widow. This was a low-mass star that's orbited by a brown dwarf. The wobble was too small in amplitude to be anything else."
paras.zh: 豪斯霍尔德说：“这是这个系统的真正关键。” “当我们测量这种摆动时，我们发现我们没有看到黑寡妇。这是一颗由褐矮星围绕的低质量恒星。摆动的幅度太小，不可能是其他任何东西。”

paras.en: The observations revealed two unusually compact objects orbiting at an extremely close distance.
paras.zh: 观测结果显示两个异常紧凑的物体以极近的距离运行。

paras.en: The central star has approximately 85 times the mass of Jupiter, while the brown dwarf weighs about 25 Jupiter masses. For comparison, the Sun is more than 1,000 times as massive as Jupiter.
paras.zh: 中央恒星的质量约为木星的 85 倍，而褐矮星的质量约为木星的 25 倍。相比之下，太阳的质量是木星的 1000 多倍。

paras.en: The brown dwarf completes a full revolution around its host star in just 87 minutes. Its entire orbit is so small that it would fit within the diameter of the Sun.
paras.zh: 这颗褐矮星在短短 87 分钟内就完成了围绕主星的完整公转。它的整个轨道非常小，可以容纳在太阳的直径之内。

paras.en: That extraordinarily close arrangement suggested that gravity might be doing more than simply keeping the objects in orbit. The researchers suspected that the star could be actively pulling matter away from the brown dwarf.
paras.zh: 这种极其紧密的排列表明，引力可能不仅仅只是将物体保持在轨道上。研究人员怀疑这颗恒星可能正在积极地将物质从褐矮星中拉走。

paras.en: Scientists Discover a New Form of Stellar Cannibalism
paras.zh: 科学家发现恒星同类相食的新形式

paras.en: When one astronomical object draws gas or other material from another, astronomers call the process accretion.
paras.zh: 当一个天体从另一个天体吸取气体或其他物质时，天文学家将这一过程称为吸积。

paras.en: Accretion is especially familiar in systems involving black holes and neutron stars. Although these objects can be extremely massive, their physical dimensions are relatively small. Material falling toward a black hole, for example, often forms a swirling disk around it before moving inward.
paras.zh: 吸积在涉及黑洞和中子星的系统中尤其常见。尽管这些物体可能非常巨大，但它们的物理尺寸相对较小。例如，落向黑洞的物质在向内移动之前通常会在黑洞周围形成一个旋转盘。

paras.en: But ZTF J0440+2325 appears to work differently.
paras.zh: 但 ZTF J0440+2325 的工作方式似乎有所不同。

paras.en: Rather than a black hole or neutron star collecting matter, an ordinary low-mass star is receiving material from a nearby brown dwarf. Because the star has a much larger physical surface than a compact object such as a black hole, the incoming material can strike it directly.
paras.zh: 一颗普通的低质量恒星不是从黑洞或中子星收集物质，而是从附近的褐矮星接收物质。由于恒星的物理表面比黑洞等致密物体大得多，因此传入的物质可以直接撞击它。

paras.en: "The difference here is, the thing absorbing matter is not a tiny black hole but a star, which is relatively big in size," Burdge explains. "So matter just pummels directly onto the surface, at very high speeds, like an asteroid hitting the Moon."
paras.zh: “这里的区别在于，吸收物质的不是一个微小的黑洞，而是一颗体积相对较大的恒星，”伯奇解释道。 “所以物质只是以非常高的速度直接撞击到表面，就像小行星撞击月球一样。”

paras.en: To investigate whether this was actually happening, the researchers created computer simulations of the system.
paras.zh: 为了调查这是否真的发生，研究人员创建了该系统的计算机模拟。

paras.en: They modeled particles originating from the brown dwarf and calculated how those particles would move under the gravitational influence of both objects. The simulations incorporated the measured properties of the star and its companion, along with the physical equations governing orbital motion.
paras.zh: 他们对源自褐矮星的粒子进行了建模，并计算了这些粒子在两个天体的引力影响下将如何移动。模拟结合了恒星及其伴星的测量特性，以及控制轨道运动的物理方程。

paras.en: The results supported the team's suspicion. Material leaving the brown dwarf followed trajectories that carried it directly into the star.
paras.zh: 结果支持了团队的怀疑。离开褐矮星的物质遵循将其直接带入恒星的轨迹。

paras.en: "When we track those test particles, we see they indeed fall right onto the surface of the star," Householder says. "This is the first time we've caught a low-mass star actively accreting from another low-mass object."
paras.zh: 豪斯霍尔德说：“当我们追踪这些测试粒子时，我们发现它们确实直接落在恒星表面。” “这是我们第一次发现一颗低质量恒星从另一个低质量天体中积极吸积。”

paras.en: A Cosmic Feast That Could Continue for Billions of Years
paras.zh: 一场可能持续数十亿年的宇宙盛宴

paras.en: The team also estimated how quickly the brown dwarf is losing material.
paras.zh: 研究小组还估计了褐矮星失去物质的速度。

paras.en: According to their calculations, the star is consuming approximately one hundred-thousandth of Earth's mass every year.
paras.zh: 根据他们的计算，这颗恒星每年消耗的质量约为地球质量的十万分之一。

paras.en: That amount may sound insignificant, but it represents an enormous quantity of material. The researchers compare it to approximately 40 million dump trucks' worth of matter, or about 1.3 trillion one-pound burritos every second.
paras.zh: 这个数量听起来微不足道，但它代表了巨大的材料数量。研究人员将其与大约 4000 万辆自卸卡车的物质进行比较，或者每秒大约 1.3 万亿个一磅的卷饼。

paras.en: Despite those staggering figures, the brown dwarf is so massive that this material loss represents only a tiny portion of its total mass.
paras.zh: 尽管有这些惊人的数字，但棕矮星的质量如此之大，以至于这种物质损失只占其总质量的一小部分。

paras.en: In astronomical terms, the feeding process is remarkably gradual.
paras.zh: 从天文学角度来看，进食过程是非常渐进的。

paras.en: Based on the properties of the system and the estimated rate of mass transfer, researchers believe the star could continue drawing matter from its companion for billions of years.
paras.zh: 根据系统的特性和估计的质量转移速率，研究人员认为这颗恒星可以在数十亿年的时间内继续从其伴星中吸取物质。

paras.en: Instead of a sudden, catastrophic collision that destroys the smaller object, the star appears to be sustaining a relatively steady flow of material from its neighbor.
paras.zh: 这颗恒星并没有发生突然的、灾难性的碰撞来摧毁较小的天体，而是似乎维持着来自其邻居的相对稳定的物质流。

paras.en: That realization also helped explain the strange triangular light pattern that first attracted Burdge's attention.
paras.zh: 这种认识也有助于解释最初引起伯奇注意的奇怪的三角形光图案。

paras.en: As matter streams from the brown dwarf toward the star, it strikes the stellar surface at high speeds, generating an intensely heated region.
paras.zh: 当物质从褐矮星流向恒星时，它会高速撞击恒星表面，产生一个高度加热的区域。

paras.en: This bright hotspot acts like a persistent fireball on the star.
paras.zh: 这个明亮的热点就像恒星上的一个持久的火球。

paras.en: As the brown dwarf moves through its 87-minute orbit, the hotspot repeatedly rotates into and out of the observer's view. Those changes in visibility produce the distinctive pattern of brightening and dimming that the astronomers had struggled to understand.
paras.zh: 当褐矮星运行 87 分钟的轨道时，热点会反复旋转进出观察者的视野。这些能见度的变化产生了天文学家一直难以理解的独特的变亮和变暗模式。

paras.en: "It's like you've got this continuous fireball onto one of the objects, and as one orbits the other, that hotspot comes in and out of view, and the peak of the triangle signal is when you're looking right at the fireball," Burdge explains.
paras.zh: 伯奇解释说：“就好像你把这个连续的火球落在其中一个物体上，当一个物体绕着另一个物体运行时，热点会进出视野，而三角形信号的峰值就是当你正视火球时。”

paras.en: A Strange Star System Opens a New Window Into Planetary Evolution
paras.zh: 一个奇怪的恒星系统为行星演化打开了一个新窗口

paras.en: With the triangular signal finally explained, the researchers are now interested in identifying other stellar systems that behave in similar ways.
paras.zh: 随着三角信号的最终解释，研究人员现在有兴趣识别具有类似行为方式的其他恒星系统。

paras.en: Until now, observations of close interactions between stars and their planetary companions have largely emphasized either stable orbits or relatively rapid engulfment events.
paras.zh: 到目前为止，对恒星与其行星伴星之间密切相互作用的观察主要强调稳定的轨道或相对快速的吞噬事件。

paras.en: ZTF J0440+2325 demonstrates that another possibility exists. Under the right conditions, a small star can steadily extract matter from a nearby brown dwarf without immediately destroying it.
paras.zh: ZTF J0440+2325表明存在另一种可能性。在适当的条件下，一颗小恒星可以稳定地从附近的褐矮星中提取物质，而不会立即摧毁它。

paras.en: Finding additional examples could help astronomers determine how common this process is, how long it can persist, and what ultimately happens to objects trapped in such extraordinarily close relationships.
paras.zh: 找到更多的例子可以帮助天文学家确定这个过程有多常见，它可以持续多久，以及陷入如此密切关系的物体最终会发生什么。

paras.en: The discovery may also provide new insights into the evolution of planets and brown dwarfs that orbit near their host stars.
paras.zh: 这一发现还可能为了解围绕其主恒星运行的行星和棕矮星的演化提供新的见解。

paras.en: "It's inspiring a lot of new searches on our part," Householder says. "I think we're going to learn a lot about a different kind of way that planets and brown dwarfs interact with their host stars."
paras.zh: “这激发了我们很多新的搜索，”豪斯霍尔德说。 “我认为我们将学到很多关于行星和棕矮星与其主恒星相互作用的不同方式。”

paras.en: This research received partial support from the National Science Foundation.
paras.zh: 这项研究得到了美国国家科学基金会的部分支持。

paras.en: Materials provided by Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Original written by Jennifer Chu. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由麻省理工学院提供。原创作者：朱珍妮。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。
